title: Migrate Go products API from monolithic handler to http.ServeMux routing
description: A Go products API uses a single Handler function with manual URL/method dispatch. Migrate to http.NewServeMux() with per-route handler registration.

task_spec.prompt:
The products package in internal/products/products.go has a single exported Handler function that manually dispatches requests by inspecting r.URL.Path and r.Method with a switch statement. Migrate it to use http.NewServeMux():

1. Keep the four private handler functions (listProducts, createProduct, getProduct, deleteProduct) with their existing logic unchanged.

2. Replace the monolithic Handler function with a NewMux() function that constructs and returns an *http.ServeMux with all four routes registered:
   - mux.HandleFunc("GET /products", listProducts)
   - mux.HandleFunc("POST /products", createProduct)
   - mux.HandleFunc("GET /products/{id}", getProduct)
   - mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /products/{id}", deleteProduct)
   Note: Go 1.22+ method+path pattern syntax is available.

3. Inside getProduct and deleteProduct, extract the {id} path value using r.PathValue("id") instead of strings.TrimPrefix.

4. Update the test file to call products.NewMux() and use httptest.NewServer(mux) or pass requests directly via mux.ServeHTTP(w, r). Remove the old Handler-based calls. All four existing tests must pass.

5. Remove the now-unused imports (strings) if applicable.

Run go test ./... and go build ./... to confirm.
required_artifacts: All 4 existing tests pass via mux.ServeHTTP
success_criteria: Route dispatch handled by stdlib ServeMux, not manual switch
All tests pass with updated test setup
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `go test ./...` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
